_comment: The Self-Host template. Every value here is a placeholder and none of them is CloudWerk's:
a Self-Host deployment is a different host and a different Entra ID app registration, and
Teams single sign-on does not support several domains per app - so the package CloudWerk
publishes cannot authenticate against your deployment at all (ADR-0011).
Copy this file, fill in your own values, and run:
pwsh ./scripts/New-TodoWerkTeamsAppPackage.ps1 -ValuesPath ./my-values.json
ManifestId       A GUID you generate once and never change. It is the identity every tenant
that installs the package records; changing it later is a tenant-by-tenant
uninstall, not a deploy.
Host             The host TodoWerk answers on, with no scheme and no trailing slash. It also
decides four addresses in the manifest, all served by your deployment itself:
privacyUrl and termsOfUseUrl (/legal/privacy and /legal/terms), websiteUrl
(/about - the page the Teams admin centre shows as the app's support link) and
publisherDocsUrl (/administrators - the page for the administrator deciding
whether to allow it). Set Legal__Operator on the deployment so all four name
you rather than nobody - see docs/runbooks/deploying-a-self-host.md.
ClientId         The application (client) id of your Entra ID app registration.
DeveloperName    Your organisation's legal name. It is what the admin centre of every tenant
that installs your package shows as the publisher, so it has to be yours
rather than CloudWerk's. The build refuses to run while it still reads
'Your organisation'.
ApplicationIdUri The Application ID URI you set on it: api://<Host>/<ClientId>.
MpnId            Optional. Your Microsoft Partner Network id, at most 10 characters. Leave it
empty unless you are already in the Partner Network - the property is then
omitted from the manifest rather than emitted blank.
Version          Semantic version of the package. Increase it whenever you re-upload.
